title: fix(app-shell): read objects by name on an empty-package app's object routes and on declared record pages (objectui#13046)
body:
Fixes #13046
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`@object-ui/app-shell`'s `readAppObjectScope` (`packages/app-shell/src/console/appObjectScope.ts`) stops falling back to the whole object registry (`GET /api/v1/meta/object`) on two route shapes the card measured on cloud's control plane:

- **An object's route in an app whose package holds none of its objects.** When the app's `meta/object?package=` read answers 0 objects, an object route (`:objectName`, `:objectName/view/:viewId`) now goes down the same by-name path a package app already uses for objects outside its package: the route's object, its lookup and master-detail targets, and the app's `requiresObject` entries, one by-name read each (joined through the adapter cache since objectui#13044). Only the route's object holds the route. The app's root (`/apps/APP`) keeps today's path: package list, then the whole registry.
- **A record route whose record page is declared.** `:objectName/record/:recordId` and its named-page sibling (`RECORD_NAMED_PAGE_ROUTE`) join `APP_OBJECT_SCOPE_ROUTES`. Once the page list has answered, the route picks the record page `RecordDetailView` renders (the named page when it is a record page of the object; else the object's default record page through `defaultRecordPageObject`, else its first record page, as `usePageAssignment` picks). For a **full** page it reads the objects that page binds through `readPageObjectScope`, the way page routes do (`pageObjectNames`), plus the route object and the app's `requiresObject` entries. With no declared page, or a **slotted** one, it reads the whole registry: the synthesized page derives its related lists from every object that points at the record's object. Nothing is read while the page list is out, so a record route that turns out to have no declared page asks exactly the requests it asked before.

`AppContent.tsx` hands the page list to `readAppObjectScope` (one callback, called only on a record route). `MetadataProvider.tsx` and `ConsoleShell.tsx` are unchanged. No new export; no server change.

## Premise check: Setup has an app package, and it holds no objects

The dispatch's ruling 3 describes Setup as having no app package. On objectstack `e4ec6ec`, `packages/apps/setup/src/index.ts` registers the Setup app under package `com.objectstack.setup` (`SETUP_APP_PACKAGE_ID`), whose manifest carries the app and no objects. objectui#12811's PR measured the same thing live ("one empty `?package=` answer, then the whole list"). So Setup has exactly the cloud app's shape (cloud's `app-cloud` header says it mirrors `@objectstack/setup`), and "a package-scoped answer of 0" does not tell them apart.

What keeps Setup's measured open unchanged is the route, not the package: objectui#12811 measured Setup's **landing** (`/apps/setup`), where by-name reads cost 11 calls and the landing loaded the whole registry anyway. This PR keeps the app root on the whole-registry path, so that open asks what it asked before (pinned below). **Setup's object routes (`/apps/setup/sys_user` and similar) do change**: they now read their object, its lookup targets and Setup's `requiresObject` entries by name instead of the whole registry. On objectstack `e4ec6ec` the plugins' Setup navigation contributions carry 12 `requiresObject` entries (a one-time grep count, not checked entry by entry and not re-derived by anything). The route waits only for its own object. That is a request-count increase and a byte decrease on those routes. It is raised for the seat in the report's `open_questions`.

## Tests

New pin `packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/AppContent.emptyPackageScope-13046.test.tsx` (real `MetadataProvider` under the real `AppContent`, client double recording each call as its URL reads), 8 tests:

- (a) `/apps/cloud/sys_environment`, package answers 0: no whole-registry read when the route first renders or after it settles; calls are exactly the package list plus `object/sys_environment`, `object/sys_organization`, `object/sys_user` (lookup targets) and `object/sys_member` (`requiresObject`).
- (b) a record route with a declared full record page: in a package app, the package list and `object/crm_quote` (bound outside the package) only; in the empty-package app, the record object, the page's objects and their lookup targets by name; the named-page route likewise.
- (c) CONTROLs, request lists counted exactly: Setup's open `/apps/setup` asks `object?package=com.objectstack.setup` then `object`; an app whose package holds its objects asks the package list and its lookup target; a record route with no declared page asks `object`; a slotted record page asks `object`.

Updated pin `AppContent.objectScope-12811.test.tsx`: its control "an app whose package holds no objects of its own reads the whole registry" asserted the old behaviour on an object route; it now asserts it on the app's root, the shape this card keeps.

**Ablation** (one-time, no file kept): `appObjectScope.ts` replaced by its blob at the base `bc98626ed5` (on-disk hash `e761114c` = base blob), the new pin run: 4 failed (both (a) and all three (b)), 4 passed (the four controls, so they assert today's requests). Restored with `git checkout HEAD`: on-disk hash `5f143758` = HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Gates

At `87ee82176f` unless noted. Exit codes captured before any pipe.

- Closure build `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/app-shell^...`: 28/28 tasks, exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check` (`tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, which includes the tests): exit 0, at `494be26b25` (same source; the next commit adds only the changeset).
- Targeted vitest, `--maxWorkers=1`, under the shared lock: the new and updated pins, plus every test file naming `appObjectScope`, `readPageObjectScope` or `AppContent`: 60 files, 496 tests, all passed (app-shell 46 files / 336 tests; apps/console and i18n 14 files / 160 tests).
- `eslint --no-inline-config` on the 4 changed files: 0 errors; warnings equal the base on the three existing files (10, 44, 3); the new test file has 3 `no-explicit-any`, the sibling pin's idiom.
- Battery, all exit 0: `check:phantom-deps`, `check:self-import`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:doc-example-readers`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:side-effects-array`, `check:element-data-source-declaration`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:action-forward-parity`, `check:designer-field-key-parity`, `check:icon-record-names`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:test-path-roots`, `scripts/check-hand-rolled-comment-mask.mjs`, `scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`.
- `check:spec-floors`: exit 1, `no-artifact` (it needs the whole workspace built); recorded, not fixed, as dispatched.

Declared to CI: the full `packages/app-shell/` and `apps/console/` directories (not run locally: the container's test lock is shared).

## Acceptance notes

- NOT MEASURED: a live open of cloud's 环境 list and an environment record, and live before/after opens of Setup and HotCRM. Reason: no cloud or HotCRM stack was run in this container; the request lists above are counted in the provider harness, not in a browser.
- HotCRM, read from its source (`objectstack-ai/hotcrm` `850f75c`): `crm_opportunity`, `crm_lead` and `crm_case` declare full record pages, so their record routes now read the package list plus the bound objects outside it; `crm_account`'s record page is slotted and keeps the whole registry.
- A record route without a declared page now issues its whole-registry read after the page list answers rather than beside it. The request set is unchanged (pinned); the two reads are serial on that route. NOT MEASURED in time.
- The console root's prefetch (`useAppObjectScopePrefetch`) is not handed the page list, so on a record route the scope starts from `AppContent`, one permission round trip after the console root.
- Only the route stand-ins (`ObjectView`, `RecordDetailView`) are mocked in the pin; a reader inside the real record view that reads `useMetadata().objects` on its own is outside what this pin sees. The census `openPathObjectReaders-12811` still passes.
